subject: Unit-price sensitivity & MAP pivot: final eval plan and close timeline
messages:
From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@pulsehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: PulseHealth Procurement <procurement@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Unit-price sensitivity & MAP pivot: final eval plan and close timeline

Hi Karthik + Marissa,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. Our execs reviewed the initial MAP and asked us to tighten the unit-econ gates before we commit to a pilot. Two quick asks so we can decide this week:

1) Can Redwood show a short-run projection of tokens/$ under our traffic mix (avg prompt length ~220 tokens, 12k daily queries, 98th pct latency < 400ms) with and without prefix caching?
2) What batching assumptions would you recommend to preserve the latency SLO while improving tokens/$?

I attached the MAP draft (v3) and our preliminary run-rate forecast. If we can get a short written plan, procurement will decide whether to proceed to contract.

Attachments: pulsehealth_map_draft_v3.pdf, pulsehealth_runrate_forecast.csv

—Alex
Alex Geller
Director of Product, PulseHealth
alex.geller@pulsehealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unit-price sensitivity & MAP pivot: final eval plan and close timeline

Alex —

Appreciate the clarity. We've run a quick sensitivity pass and can deliver a concise addendum to the MAP that shows:

- Tokens per USD across three operating points (baseline, with KV prefix cache, with 64ms batching window)
- Latency impact at P95/P99 for each operating point
- Suggested rollout: 2-week evaluation (functional correctness), 2-week performance run (traffic shadowing), final gated decision for pilot billing model

A few details that would help make the numbers precise:
- Confirm the traffic distribution (peak vs off-peak) — is the 12k/day concentrated in a 10-hour window or flatter?
- Do you have a target for average tokens per response after instruction tuning/templating? You mentioned ~220 prompt tokens; do we expect ~60-120 completion tokens typically?

Draft timeline proposal (can compress if you need a faster close):
- Jun 24: Share conservative tokens/$ worksheet and assumptions (we'll attach token_econ_model.xlsx)
- Jun 26: Run a 48-hour shadow test with your sample traffic (prefetch & cache enabled)
- Jun 28: Performance readout and MAP update (final gating numbers)
- Jun 30: Procurement decision window / signature (DocuSign link)

I'll attach the model now — it contains knobs for cache hit rate, batching latency window, and quantization profile. Quick note on assumptions baked into the model:
- Baseline serving uses q4_0 quantization on our optimized runtime
- KV prefix cache hit-rate scenarios modeled at 10%, 30%, 60%
- Batching: we model both continuous batching (micro-batch size determined by 16ms waiting or 64ms waiting) and request coalescing; we report latency percentiles for each.

If that timeline works, Marissa/Ben/Laura and I will own the technical run and the readout.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jun 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unit-price sensitivity & MAP pivot: final eval plan and close timeline

Alex — quick follow from our side and a suggestion to tighten gating so procurement can sign:

On Wed, Jun 21, 2028 at 09:03 Karthik Iyer wrote:
> A few details that would help make the numbers precise:
> - Confirm the traffic distribution (peak vs off-peak) — is the 12k/day concentrated in a 10-hour window or flatter?

We typically treat the gating as two checks: cost/unit and SLA risk. Proposed concrete gates:
- Cost gate: tokens/$ at or below $0.0018 (baseline) OR tokens/$ <= $0.0025 with 30% prefix cache + 64ms batching window.
- SLA gate: P99 latency <= 550ms during the 48-hour shadow test with production headers. If P99 exceeds this, fallback to a smaller model variant for peak windows.

Operational asks (for PulseHealth):
- Share 3 days of anonymized sample traffic (JSON lines) with typical prompt/completion tokens; we will run a deterministic simulation in the token_econ_model.xlsx and our internal profiler.
- Confirm if procurement will accept a usage-commit + overage pricing (we can draft the DocuSign template).

I attached a cleaned slice of assumption notes into the MAP draft (see updated section 4). If you want, Ben can own the shadow test orchestration — Ben?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@pulsehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: PulseHealth Procurement <procurement@pulsehealth.com>, Eve Martin <eve.martin@finops-consult.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jun 2028 13:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Unit-price sensitivity & MAP pivot: final eval plan and close timeline

Thanks — we can provide the 72-hour sample slice by EOD tomorrow and procurement is ok with a usage-commit + overage structure (they want explicit unit-econ thresholds in the SOW). Eve from our advisors is on copy and will validate the model inputs.

Attached is the run-rate forecast (lightly redacted). We'd like the shadow test to run the week of Jun 26. Can we do a 30-minute sync tomorrow to confirm ports/keys and the anonymization format?

Attachments: pulsehealth_runrate_forecast.csv

—Alex
Alex Geller
Director of Product, PulseHealth
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@pulsehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2028 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unit-price sensitivity & MAP pivot: final eval plan and close timeline

Alex — all good. Quick confirmation and next steps:

- We received the run-rate file and the anonymized sample (thanks). Our team kicked off the deterministic simulation against token_econ_model.xlsx; preliminary numbers expected tomorrow morning.
- Shadow test scheduled: Jun 27 00:00 UTC — Jun 29 23:59 UTC (48h with two dry-run windows included). Ben will coordinate ports and test keys; Laura will run the latency analytics and produce P95/P99 charts.
- MAP milestones (mutual action plan):
  * Jun 24: Conservative tokens/$ worksheet shared (delivered)
  * Jun 27–29: Shadow test (technical validation)
  * Jun 30: Final gates readout + procurement decision window

If the gating numbers (tokens/$ + P99) meet the thresholds Marissa proposed, we will prepare the DocuSign SOW with the usage-commit + overage terms. I'll send the DocuSign link as soon as the readout completes.

Meeting: 30-min readout scheduled for Jun 30 16:00 UTC — calendar invite to follow.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this one.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: token_econ_model.xlsx
